name: Ju
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1, languoid juuu1243 'Ju' (HTML page and JSON record), plus reference records 76828 and 569683 and the pages for guru1272, tala1296, sout3161, tala1295, zang1255, kirb1236, mang1416.
sources.note: Bibliographic only: the two Glottolog's most extensive descriptions for Ju are both 'a wordlist or less' (Decker et al. 2022; Shimizu 1978); the Guruntumic, Tala-Sho-Zangwal and South Bauchi East group pages cite only Shimizu 1978; no grammar, sketch or phonology exists for Ju in Glottolog.
Nothing; cites only Ethnologue 25, Blench 2006 AALIST, Blench 2012 Atlas, Blench 2021 West Chadic classification, OLAC and Glottolog. Notes 'The language is unwritten.'

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. South Bauchi languages page (rogerblench.info/Language/Afroasiatic/Chadic/West/B3/SBOP.htm), Internet Archive copy 2024-07-24.
sources.note: Nothing on Ju; the page offers materials only for Mantsi, Megang, Zul, Gyazi, Dyarim, Gere and Goji. rogerblench.info itself is behind a captcha.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, Yakubu Danladi, Luther Hon, Adedamola Aregbesola, Thelma Araokanmi, John Muniru & David Onoja. 2022. A Sociolinguistic Profile of Some Endangered West Chadic B.3 Languages in South Bauchi State, Nigeria with Notes on Dulubu [dbo]. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2022-019. SIL International. 73 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sections 8.3 'Phonetic inventories' (consonants, 5-8 vowel system, vowel length) and 8.5.1 'Phonological variation between Juu, Tala, and Zamwar' (pp. 28-30: b~p, d~t, g~k, final ŋ~n, final i~Ø correspondences) contain no prosodic statement; the word 'stress' does not occur in the document. Appendix F (p. 49) says the 222-item wordlists (Bauchi Juu, Dass Juu) are preliminary 'since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features'; entries carry pitch diacritics but no tone or stress analysis. Its only prior sources for Juu are Shimizu (1978) and Som…

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2012 [2011]. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, 3rd ed. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation / Mallam Dendo.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Entry 222 'Ju' (p. 45) gives only: Bauchi State, Bauchi LGA; 150 (LA 1971); Chadic: West sub-branch B: Zaar group: Guruntum subgroup. No sources or descriptive work listed.

sources.citation: Jaggar, Philip J. 1988. Guruntum (gùrdùŋ) (West Chadic-B): linguistic notes and wordlist. African Languages and Cultures 1(2): 169-189.

sources.note: Sketch of the sister language Guruntum with tone-marked wordlist; may mention Ju/Sho in its survey of the subgroup. Proxy only.

sources.citation: Haruna, Andrew. 2003. A Grammatical Outline of Gùrdùŋ/Gùrùntùm (Southern Bauchi, Nigeria). LINCOM Studies in African Linguistics 62. Munich: LINCOM Europa. 160 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Closest relative with a full description (Guruntum-Mbaaru, same Guruntumic subgroup); its tone/prosody chapter is the best proxy for what a Ju description would say, but it does not describe Ju itself.

sources.citation: Shimizu, Kiyoshi. 1978. The Southern Bauchi group of Chadic languages: a survey report. Africana Marburgensia Sonderheft 2. Marburg/Lahn: Africana Marburgensia. 48 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only other primary source on Ju ('Sho'); a comparative wordlist survey of the whole South Bauchi group that may carry tone marking and general remarks on the prosody of the group. Unlikely to contain a stress rule but it is the one document a Ju phonology note could hide
